findings.message: 096 AC-4 now checks `releasedAt` in two different ways depending on the path. In `SyncInput` it must be a datetime with an offset, but the push's `SpecRecordInput` (push.ts:36) still accepts any `text(40)`, and the reader (sync/specclaw.ts:96) passes `phases.archived.at` through without normalising it. The push never parses `SyncInput`, so it accepts anything and `knownTime` turns it into a stored value or null. The self-sync goes through `syncProposal`'s service input, so the same record throws a ZodError. `syncSpecclaw` (sync/import.ts:121) rethrows anything that isn't a `KeyTakenError`, so the whole run stops partway. Records already written stay committed, and `markSynced` and withdrawals never run. Fix: use one rule. Normalise `releasedAt` once where the write is built (`desired()`), for example to ISO when `Date.parse` succeeds and to null otherwise, the same way `phaseTimesOf` handles phase times. Then give the push's `SpecRecordInput` and `SyncInput` the same schema. Add a table test that drives both push and self-sync with a date-only value, a value with no offset, and a future value.
findings.scenario: An archived change's state.json has `phases.archived.at: "2026-10-18"` (date only) or `"2026-10-18T10:00:00"` (no offset). `sync_specclaw` stores it, but `pnpm --filter @amax/delivery sync:specclaw` throws a ZodError on that record and stops. Proposals after it aren't synced, unchanged ones keep their old stale mark, and gone folders aren't withdrawn.

findings.message: `READ` is a third copy of the `<ref>@<sha>` rule, and it disagrees with the others. `sync/withdraw.ts:6` and `sync/authors.ts:14` accept any prefix before `@<sha>`, while `READ` (`^[^@\s]+@SHA$`) rejects a ref that itself contains `@`, which git allows. `entries()` also applies `readOf` to stored entries, and since `out` starts from `before`, every later write saves those sources as null for good. Fix: export one read matcher from `sync/sha.ts` and use it in all three places. Keep a stored source as it is rather than rewriting it to null.
findings.scenario: A push from branch `team@x/096-y` with sha `abc1234` has meta.source `team@x/096-y@abc1234`. Withdrawal treats it as a ref@sha, but `readOf` returns null, so the verify phase's history line names no read. On the next write, the stored entry's source is saved as null.

findings.message: The AC-4 `releasedAt` bound is tested only through `syncProposal`, and with two variants. The push (`sync_specclaw` → `upsertSpecProposal`) is the main writer and has no test for a future or malformed `releasedAt`, so 'every writer' isn't shown. Add push-path rows for a future time, a time with no offset, and a past time.
